summary: HyperText Markup Language: the semantic skeleton, document tree, and accessibility foundation of the web.

rows.means: tells the browser to render using modern HTML5 standards
rows.consequence: Required at the absolute first line of every HTML file. Without it, browsers trigger legacy 'quirks mode', breaking modern CSS box-sizing and layout standards.

rows.means: the root document element wrapping everything
rows.consequence: The lang attribute is critical: screen readers use it for phonetic pronunciation, and search engines use it for geo-targeted indexing.

rows.means: metadata container / visible user interface container
rows.consequence: <head> holds machine data (title, meta, styles, scripts). <body> holds all rendered markup visible to the end user.
Ensures characters from all human alphabets, symbols, and emojis render correctly without garbled mojibake symbols.

rows.means: instructs mobile browsers to scale to the device screen width
rows.consequence: Without this single line, mobile phones render desktop-width pages at 980px zoom, causing tiny illegible text and horizontal scrolling.

rows.means: sets browser tab title and search engine snippet title
rows.consequence: Crucial for both browser bookmarks and search results; also announced first by assistive screen reading technology.

rows.means: imports external CSS stylesheets into the document
rows.consequence: Placed in the head so styles are applied before the text is painted, which is what prevents the unstyled flash a reader sees when a sheet arrives late.

rows.means: loads external JavaScript asynchronously without blocking HTML parsing
rows.consequence: The defer attribute downloads scripts in parallel with HTML parsing and executes them in document order once parsing completes.
Landmark elements allow screen readers and keyboard users to jump directly across major page sections without navigating every individual link.

rows.means: self-contained reusable unit / thematic content grouping
rows.consequence: <article> represents content that makes sense on its own (e.g. blog post, card). <section> represents a thematic chapter with a heading.
Used for sidebars, callout boxes, related links, or advertising. Screen readers treat it as secondary content.

rows.means: six levels of document heading hierarchy
rows.consequence: Never skip heading levels (e.g. h1 to h3) for styling. Use CSS for font size, and reserve headings for the document outline.
Browsers apply default vertical paragraph margins to enforce typographic rhythm and readability.
When opening in a new tab (_blank), rel="noopener noreferrer" prevents the new window from accessing window.opener for tab-napping exploits.
Unlike a div with a click handler, it is reachable by keyboard, activates on the usual keys without code, and is announced as a button by a screen reader.
Groups inputs and owns submission, including submission from the keyboard and the validation the browser performs before anything is sent.

rows.means: text label programmatically bound to an input
rows.consequence: The for attribute matches the input's id. Clicking the label focuses the input, expanding the touch/click target area.
Specifying the correct type enables built-in client validation, mobile keyboards (e.g. numeric keypad for type="number" or "tel"), and secure password masking.
Unlike <input>, maintains multiple lines of user prose. Preserves newline characters upon submission.
Allows user to pick one or more options from a fixed list. The selected option's value is sent upon form submit.
Use <th> with scope="col" or scope="row" so assistive screen readers read column headers aloud alongside cell data.

rows.means: unordered list (bullets) / ordered list (numbered) / list item
rows.consequence: Tells a screen reader how many items are in the set before it starts reading them, which is the difference between navigating a list and wading through a stack of anonymous containers.
The alt attribute describes the image for blind users and when images fail to load. loading="lazy" defers offscreen downloads.

rows.means: art direction and responsive image switching
rows.consequence: Offers newer formats first and falls back to the widely supported one, or swaps the crop entirely between a phone and a desktop — the choice being made by the browser, which knows things the author does not.
Eliminated legacy third-party plugins. Supports multiple <source> formats and subtitles via <track kind="subtitles">.

rows.means: bitmapped pixel canvas for 2D/3D graphics and games
rows.consequence: Provides a JavaScript drawing context (CanvasRenderingContext2D or WebGL) for immediate-mode graphics.
Resolution-independent vector graphics defined mathematically via XML paths; sharp on any display density.
The sandbox attribute restricts scripts, forms, and popups to prevent malicious third-party embeds from attacking the host page.
Handles the backdrop, keeps keyboard focus inside the dialog while it is open, and closes on the usual key, none of which has to be written by hand.
Toggles visibility of child content natively without any JavaScript or CSS state management.

rows.means: accessibility attributes describing state and role
rows.consequence: Communicates dynamic changes — a menu opening, a region loading — to assistive technology, which otherwise sees only the markup and not what changed.

rows.means: stores custom private data directly on HTML elements
rows.consequence: Accessible in JavaScript via element.dataset.userId and in CSS selectors via [data-user-id="42"].
